title: Arcadia Freight pilot ask + objection map
body:
Context / short summary:
- Arcadia Freight: mid-market freight forwarding + TMS provider. Potential pilot to benchmark inference for automated ETA & SLA communication features (customer portal notifications, dispatcher chat assist).
- Goal: 6-week technical pilot to validate latency (<150ms p95), cost/unit targets, and quality (>85% intent match on 3 prompt suites).

Notes to self / quick signals:
- They run a multi-cloud stack (GCP + private on-prem DBs) — will likely insist on VPC peering or private deployment.
- Security + SOC2 questions are going to be first blocker. Have Redwood Private checklist handy.
- Current pain: manual ETA updates, customer support load on simple inquiries (where is shipment, ETA change?), reuse of templates across accounts.
- Possible pilot champions: Head of Ops (Jen L.), Platform Eng (Ravi P.), Head of Product (Elena M.). Need intro via LinkedIn or warm intro from Luke (customer success).

Pilot ask (concise):
- 6-week pilot: integrate Redwood Private (single-tenant) into a staging TMS environment.
- Deliverables: automated ETA suggestion endpoint + a small agent to draft customer-facing ETA change messages; dashboard for false positives.
- SLOs: p95 latency <150ms, error rate <2%, cost < $0.002 per inference (target).
- Data constraints: no PII stored; telemetry for quality only with hashed IDs.
- Success criteria: 20% reduction in support message load for ETA queries OR 80% acceptance rate of suggested messages by dispatchers.

Quick outbound variants (pick & A/B test):
Email - short (1):
Subject: Quick pilot to cut ETA inquiry load at Arcadia
Hi Jen —
We help freight platforms automate ETA replies and cut dispatcher messages by ~20% using a lightweight private inference pilot. Would you be open to a 20-minute call to see a short plan and timeline?
Asha

Email - value-led (2):
Subject: 6-week private pilot for ETA automation (low risk)
Hi Jen —
We saw Arcadia’s public product notes on predicted ETAs — we’ve helped similar TMS teams deploy a private inference endpoint that drafts customer-facing ETA messages and reduced support volume while keeping data in a VPC. No model data leaves your network. Can I send a two-slide plan?

LinkedIn DM (short):
Jen — quick question. Would Arcadia be interested in a 6-week private pilot to auto-suggest ETA messages and reduce manual dispatch edits? I can share a one-pager.

Voicemail script (30s):
"Hi Jen — this is Asha at Redwood Inference. We help freight platforms automate routine ETA communications with a private pilot that integrates into staging TMS. I’ll follow up with an email — would love to schedule a short intro next week. My number is 415-555-01xx."

Stakeholder map (notes):
- Jen L. (Head of Ops) — cares about reduced tickets, operator trust. Objection: "accuracy/false positives".
- Ravi P. (Platform Eng) — cares infra + security. Objection: "network architecture and data flows".
- Elena M. (Head of Product) — cares UX + adoption. Objection: "dispatcher workflow friction".
- Procurement / Legal — cares contracts, DPA, indemnity. Objection: "compliance & SLAs".

Common objections & suggested responses (quick reference):
1) "We can't send customer data to external APIs."
   - Response: "Totally — pilot runs on Redwood Private in your VPC, no payload leaves your network. We can provide architecture diagram and SOC2 evidence.
   - Tech hook: endpoint is behind your ALB, we ship a thin control plane only."

2) "How do we trust the suggestions — too many false or awkward messages?"
   - Response: "We start with read-only suggestions (dispatcher accepts/edits). We'll use your historical message templates to fine-tune prompt templates and monitor quality with a manual review cadence. Acceptance target is 80% — we stop if <60% after 2 weeks and iterate."

3) "What's the cost?"
   - Response: "Pilot pricing is fixed (6 weeks) to cover compute + integration. For production we recommend Dedicated capacity or quantized variants to hit your per-inference cost targets. We’ll share an estimated TCO model in the one-pager."

4) "We have on-prem and sensitive telemetry — can you operate air-gapped?"
   - Response: "Yes — we support on-prem private deployment; need a short tech discovery to scope. Historically takes 3–6 weeks for full air-gapped install depending on infra."

5) "We don't have engineering bandwidth."
   - Response: "Our solutions engineering team runs most of the integration work — typical eng time required: 2–3 days for initial test harness. We can also provide pre-built connectors for common TMSs."

Objection severity (internal shorthand):
- Security objections = blocker (high).
- Accuracy/UX = medium (can be mitigated with acceptance flow).
- Cost/Bandwidth = low-medium (commercial levers).

Technical prep notes (for SRE/SE call):
- Required: staging endpoint, sample anonymized messages, list of templates, expected request volume (rps), average sequence length.
- Preferred: VPC peering + EKS cluster access temporarily for sidecar install OR allow Redwood to deploy a small VM with our runtime and your control plane egress rules.
- Logging: we need to store only hashes + quality telemetry. Offer to redact PII via regex on ingest.

Quality / evaluation plan:
- Baseline: sample set of 500 ETA queries, run offline comparison between current rule-based responses and Redwood suggestions.
- Metrics: acceptance rate, avg edit length (chars changed), false-positive flag rate, time saved per ticket.
- Reporting cadence: weekly snapshot + retrospective at week 4 and week 6.

Draft pilot timeline (lean):
- Week 0: NDA + DPA + kickoff (SE + infra contact).
- Week 1: staging integration + sample data ingestion.
- Week 2: closed-loop offline evaluation (500 samples).
- Weeks 3–5: live pilot with dispatcher suggestion flow, weekly tuning.
- Week 6: review + decision (go/not go).

Open questions (to resolve before intro):
- Can they expose a staging endpoint for non-PII requests?
- Who owns data retention policy for logs?
- Any procurement thresholds for pilots > $XXk?

Conversation snippets to test (A/B quick riffs):
- "We keep the models in your network; you control logs."
- "Sample pilot: 6 weeks, fixed price, low engineering lift."
- "We measure adoption by acceptance rate not just correctness — pragmatic metric for dispatchers."

Notes for next steps (owner tags):
- Asha: prepare 1-pager + architecture diagram (due: 2025-11-07).
- Marcus: spin a quick TCO slide with dedicated vs private pricing bands (due: 2025-11-09).
- Daniel: pull SOC2 + Private deployment checklist and confirm typical install lead times (due: 2025-11-06).
- Ask Luke (CS) for a warm intro to Jen L. (if available).

Quick checklist before first call:
- [ ] 1-pager (value + ask) ready
- [ ] Architecture diagram (private deployment) ready
- [ ] Pilot contract template + DPA excerpt
- [ ] One sample set (anonymized) to run offline AS-IS
- [ ] Suggested SLOs and detection triggers

Tone notes: keep outreach short, signal low risk (private deployment), explicit minimal eng lift, emphasize dispatcher control (accept/edit flow).

Internal follow-up thoughts (brain-dump):
- If procurement balks at price, propose a revenue-share or pilot credit tied to defect reduction.
- If accuracy is a concern, propose rapid micro-iterative cycles: 2-week tuning sprints.
- Opportunity to upsell: once dispatchers accept messages, open door for more templates (claims, customs docs).

-- end --
